None used PKINIT/certificate pre-authentication, so there is no observed use of a stolen or forged certificate for authentication in this dataset. (The pbeesly TGTs from 10.0.1.4/10.0.1.6 are consistent with normal logons and do not by themselves show certificate abuse.)

T1003.reason: Credential-access tooling confirmed on scranton: hidden PowerShell stego/IEX loader (PID 2976, parent control.exe) opened lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF/0x1FFFFF, alongside SysinternalsSuite deployment, discovery, keystroke/screenshot jobs and exfil staging.

T1003.001.reason: LSASS memory access with full-access masks: PowerShell.exe 0x1FFFFF on scranton (03:05:16) and wsmprovhost.exe 0x1F3FFF on nashua (03:09:29); remaining 300+ lsass accesses are svchost/Azure-agent 0x1000/0x1400 and process-start behaviour.

T1003.002.reason: No reg save of SAM/SYSTEM/SECURITY, no 4663 access to SAM/SECURITY hives, no hive-export script blocks.

T1003.003.reason: No ntdsutil/vssadmin/ntds.dit command lines, file writes or object access; hosts are not domain controllers.

T1003.004.reason: Only Policy\Secrets\$MACHINE.ACC 4662 reads by LOCAL SERVICE (machine account), no lsadump/secretsdump activity.

T1003.005.reason: No SECURITY\Cache object access and no cache/dcc/secretsdump script blocks.

T1003.006.reason: Single 4662 replication-GUID access on newyork by the machine account NEWYORK$ with no DRSUAPI traffic or DCSync tooling; assessed benign.

T1040.reason: The only packet-capture activity is netsh.exe 'trace start capture=yes' / 'trace stop' on scranton.dmevals.local, spawned by the Microsoft Azure Network Watcher agent (NetworkWatcherAgent.exe /service) as SYSTEM using the signed Microsoft netsh.exe — legitimate platform diagnostics. No third-party sniffers (pktmon/windump/tcpdump/rawcap/dumpcap/wireshark/tshark), no Npcap/WinPcap driver image loads, no capture-driver service installs, and no capture-related traffic in the zeek window.

T1056.reason: Input capture confirmed on scranton.dmevals.local: PowerShell Invoke-ScreenCapture loop saving desktop screenshots, plus PowerShell.exe opening lsass.exe with 0x1FFFFF.

T1056.001.reason: No GetAsyncKeyState/SetWindowsHookEx/keylog script blocks, no keyboard filter driver or keylogger service installs; only default keyboard-layout registry writes.

T1056.002.reason: Invoke-ScreenCapture function (CopyFromScreen loop, 300s interval, .bmp to Downloads) defined in psversion.ps1 and invoked by pbeesly on scranton.dmevals.local.

T1056.003.reason: No wwwroot/inetpub/.aspx access, no login-portal file creation, no login/auth/signin HTTP URLs; 'login' hits were file-archive staging scripts.

T1056.004.reason: PowerShell.exe (scranton) and wsmprovhost.exe (nashua) opened lsass.exe with 0x1FFFFF/0x1F3FFF and UNKNOWN call-trace frames; remaining lsass access is benign OS/Azure perf-counter reads.

T1110.reason: Zero 4625/4771 failures; the only 4776 is a successful validation (Error Code 0x0) for pbeesly. No repeated authentication attempts on any host.

T1110.001.reason: No failed logons and no net user/net use enumeration; PowerShell password matches are module manifests/resource strings.

T1110.002.reason: No hive/NTDS/SAM dump commands or file access; lsass access is dominated by svchost/Azure agents and the 2 PowerShell accesses indicate credential theft (T1003), not cracking.

T1110.003.reason: No spray pattern; 4648 events are UMFD/DWM/machine-account logons and the single runas is a local UAC elevation by pbeesly.

T1110.004.reason: No authentication attempts across multiple accounts; hardcoded credentials in scranton PowerShell scripts relate to certificate export and WebDAV exfiltration, not stuffing.

T1111.reason: No MFA/smart-card interception artifacts: zero process creations with smart-card/credential-provider/MFA command lines in sysmon (event.code:1) and security (4688); no SCardSvr or credential-provider service/DLL installation. The only SmartCard/Credential registry writes are services.exe MuiCache entries and the built-in CredentialEnrollmentManagerUserSvc, plus lsass.exe boot-time LSA/CredentialGuard values on scranton. The 4648 explicit-credential events are pbeesly PsExec logons to NASHUA (PSEXESVC), and the 'Credential'-matching script block is an exfiltration function with a hardcoded account password — neither is MFA interception.

T1187.reason: No forced-authentication artifacts in the retrieved data. The only .lnk files are Explorer Recent items and a StartUp persistence shortcut (hostui.lnk) written by the compromised PowerShell process; all 66 outbound SMB connections are System-process traffic to internal hosts 10.0.0.4, 10.0.1.6 and fe80::e40c:95b6:b0a7:6429; 5140/5145 share access is domain machine-account SYSVOL/IPC$ plus pbeesly ADMIN$ writes for lateral movement; the sole NTLM reference is a once-per-boot LsaSrv 6038 warning; the only WebDAV usage is the attacker's own Invoke-Exfil script mapping \\192.168.0.4\webdav with hardcoded credentials to copy out an archive (exfiltration, not credential coercion). Zeek window (2020-04-30) does not overlap and shows only internal SMB file access and no WebDAV/PROPFIND HTTP.

T1212.reason: No exploit of a vulnerable service or memory-corruption payload was observed, but the compromised pbeesly PowerShell session (hidden, -ep bypass, launched from control.exe) opened lsass.exe with full-access masks 0x1f3fff/0x1fffff on scranton (sysmon EID 10 and security 4656) and wsmprovhost.exe did the same on nashua, alongside LSA registry reads and private-key/clipboard collection. No lsass dump file or MiniDump tooling was found, so credential access via exploitation is suspected but not confirmed.

T1539.reason: No access to or copying of browser cookie/credential stores: sysmon code 10 hits on browser images = 0, sysmon code 2 hits = 0, security 4663/4656 object names matching cookie/Login Data/Web Data = 0. The only cookie-related artifacts are a service-profile INetCookies file created by svchost.exe on scranton and rundll32 davclnt.dll,DavSetCookie WebDAV credential caching for the 192.168.0.4/webdav exfil share; PowerShell 4104 'Cookies/sqlite' hits are Microsoft module manifests and the screen-capture/exfil tooling, not cookie theft.

T1552.reason: Get-PrivateKeys/Invoke-Exfil PowerShell tooling on scranton.dmevals.local under pbeesly harvested certificates and embedded plaintext credentials, alongside PsExec with cleartext password to NASHUA.

T1552.001.reason: Plaintext credentials (cozy/MyCozyPassw0rd!, Fl0nk3rt0n!T0by) present in attacker scripts and command lines; no config/unattend file-content harvesting seen.

T1552.002.reason: All credential-named registry writes are OS service/identity/winlogon activity; no hive dumping or stored-credential reads.

T1552.003.reason: No ConsoleHost_history, PSReadLine or Get-History access in sysmon, powershell or security data.

T1552.004.reason: Export-PfxCertificate loop exported all LocalMachine certs to Downloads; Sysmon confirms coyn5igj.3io.pfx created by powershell.exe on SCRANTON.

T1552.006.reason: SYSVOL reads are machine-account GPO refresh (gpt.ini/GptTmpl.inf); no Groups.xml or cpassword access.

T1555.reason: PowerShell.exe on scranton opened lsass with 0x1FFFFF/0x1f3fff and an UNKNOWN call-trace module at 03:05:16 on a host showing script-based compromise; wsmprovhost on nashua also opened lsass with 0x1f3fff but its call trace matches a Get-Process cmdlet. No dump tooling, dump files or lsass object-access auditing corroborate actual dumping.

T1555.003.reason: No access to browser Login Data / Local State / logins.json / key4.db; the single cookie-file write was a Windows platform INetCookies container.

T1555.004.reason: No cmdkey/credman/vault execution, no Vault/Credentials registry or file access; only a Credential Guard configuration status message.

T1555.005.reason: No KeePass/1Password/Bitwarden process, file, memory or script activity; observed archiving is bulk file collection for exfiltration.

T1556.reason: Attacker-controlled hidden PowerShell (PID 2976, pbeesly, scranton) opened lsass with 0x1FFFFF and wsmprovhost on nashua with 0x1F3FFF, but no authentication-process modification was observed — the access is credential dumping.

T1556.001.reason: No LSA registry writes, no unexpected lsass module loads, no DC authentication patching; anomalous lsass handles are dump-style access.

T1556.002.reason: No Notification Packages registry change, no DLL dropped to System32, no password-filter references in PowerShell or windows.other.

T1556.005.reason: No 4739 events and no Reversible/UserAccountControl registry or command-line activity.

T1556.006.reason: No 4739/5136 authentication policy changes; zeek kerberos records show only routine client-to-DC authentication.

T1556.007.reason: No 5136 directory changes and no ADFS/Azure AD Connect or cloud-sync binaries loaded.

T1556.008.reason: No NetworkProvider registry writes, DLL loads or file drops; lsass handles reflect memory access, not a registered provider.

T1557.reason: No interception/relay evidence in sysmon, security or Zeek data. Outbound connections go to expected internal peers and Microsoft/Azure endpoints. The malicious PsExec+sdelete chain found on scranton/nashua is lateral movement and anti-forensics, not AiTM.

T1557.001.reason: SMB 445 and NBT-NS 137 traffic is ordinary domain traffic to 10.0.0.4; DNS queries are routine; no DNSClient registry tampering (C232 zero hits); the only NTLM network logon (172.18.39.2) is followed by type 10 logons from the same address, indicating a remote interactive session rather than a relay.

T1557.002.reason: Zeek L2 mapping is stable and one-to-one (10.0.1.6 -> 00:0d:3a:13:e3:69, 10.0.1.4 -> 00:0d:3a:4d:42:f2, responder 12:34:56:78:9a:bc consistent); no duplicate MAC for multiple IPs. arp.exe /a, route.exe print and ipconfig /all are read-only diagnostics spawned by Azure Guest Agent/Telemetry/WaAppAgent.

T1557.003.reason: DHCP-related event codes 1341/1342/1020/1063 returned zero hits and no PowerShell referenced dhcp/netsh. The NDIS Capture start-type changes on scranton are part of an Azure Network Watcher netsh trace packet capture, not DHCP spoofing.

T1558.reason: PowerShell.exe on scranton (0x1F3FFF then 0x1FFFFF) and wsmprovhost.exe on nashua (0x1F3FFF) opened lsass.exe with full-access masks alongside a hands-on-keyboard PowerShell toolkit (keystroke logging, screen capture, exfil), indicating credential access — but no Kerberos ticket theft, ticket-dumping tooling or Kerberos anomalies were observed.

T1558.001.reason: No krbtgt dumping, no 'golden'/'krbtgt'/'mimikatz' script blocks, no kdc service installs; 4768/4769 for pbeesly and machine accounts only, AES 0x12, status 0x0.

T1558.002.reason: No silver-ticket tooling or service-ticket forgery evidence; 4769 service tickets only for machine accounts/krbtgt with AES 0x12 and status 0x0.

T1558.003.reason: No Kerberoast/SPN/GetUserSPNs/Rubeus artifacts; all 4769 tickets use AES 0x12 (no RC4 0x17) and target only machine accounts; Zeek kerberos shows normal single-client AS/TGS flow.

T1558.004.reason: No AS-REP/GetNPUsers/Rubeus artifacts; all 4768 events have PreAuthType 2 with status 0x0, and Zeek AS requests are a normal pbeesly logon with one KDC_ERR_PREAUTH_REQUIRED.

T1606.reason: User-launched PowerShell (PID 2976) on scranton opened lsass.exe with 0x1F3FFF/0x1FFFFF at 03:05:16Z immediately after exporting machine certificates; other high-access lsass events are from OS processes (wininit, csrss, svchost).

T1606.001.reason: No cookie-store access or cookie-related script blocks; the single INetCookies file creation is a normal LocalService AppContainer artefact created by svchost.exe.

T1606.002.reason: Get-PrivateKeys in readme.ps1 exported every cert:\LocalMachine certificate to a .pfx with hardcoded password 'saribas' on scranton, producing C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\coyn5igj.3io.pfx — private-key theft enabling token forgery.

T1621.reason: 5 planned checks, all with zero hits

T1649.reason: On scranton.dmevals.local, user pbeesly executed a staged script (readme.txt renamed to readme.ps1 and dot-sourced) defining Get-PrivateKeys, which exported every cert:\LocalMachine certificate with Export-PfxCertificate to a randomly named .pfx in Downloads protected by hardcoded password 'saribas'; Sysmon confirmed creation of C:\Users\pbeesly\Downloads\coyn5igj.3io.pfx by powershell.exe. Certificate/private-key theft for later authentication abuse.
